To order adjectives correctly in English sentences, follow this general rule:

1. Order adjectives based on their type:
   - Quantitative adjectives (e.g., big, small, many, few): usually come first
   - Qualitative adjectives (e.g., happy, beautiful, good, bad): come next
   - Demonstrative adjectives (e.g., this, that, these, those): come next
   - Possessive adjectives (e.g., my, your, his, her): come next
   - National adjectives (e.g., American, British, Chinese): come next
   - Other adjectives (e.g., old, new, big, small): come last

2. Order adjectives within each type:
   - Order qualitative adjectives based on their meaning and intensity (e.g., beautiful > nice > good)
   - Order national adjectives based on their geographical location (e.g., American > British > Chinese)
